newsitem.title: FRANCE: Tietmeyer says EMU timetable must be kept.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer says EMU timetable must be kept.

text.p: German Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer said on Thursday that the timetable for European monetary union must be kept and that any decision on a delay would in any case not be for central bankers but for politicians.
"Concerning the timetable, it must be kept to," he said in an interview with French TF1 television to be broadcast later on Thursday, around midnight (2200 GMT).
"And if it has to be delayed, that's for the political authorities to decide, but certainly not cental banks," he said, according to a transcript in French of the interview.
"Unfortunately you have received erroneous information. I did not talk of a delay," he said in response to a comment from his interviewer that he had spoken last week of a delay to monetary union.

"I think that a monetary union would be possible only if Germany and France are part of it. This is not enshrined in the (Maastricht) treaty, it's my opinion, and as far as I know, this opinion is shared to a large extent in Europe," he said.

"Therefore, it is a question of knowing whether the two economies are in a position where we can really launch the union. And I really hope this will be the case in spring of next year when it will be discussed and decided," he said.
"If one of the two countries was not part of it, monetary union could trigger conflict and this must not happen," he said.
Asked about France, currently on the way to a May/June parliamentary election, Tietmeyer said this was not an issue for him to get involved in.

"But I would add that all of us, not just the members of the Bundesbank council, but all the German authorities, have an interest in the continuation of the process of cleaning up of the economy, and the economic development, which are underway," he said.
